articles.title: Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team
articles.pageTitle: Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team
articles.description: MEDIA ADVISORY October 6, 2026 Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announces the a
articles.pageText: Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team Press Releases Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team Share 5d ago MEDIA ADVISORY October 6, 2026 Smriti Mandhana appointed captain of Indian Women’s Cricket Team The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announces the appointment of Smriti Mandhana as the captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team. Smriti has been one of the leading figures in Indian women's cricket over the years and has played a key role in the team's progress across formats. An experienced international cricketer, she has also demonstrated her leadership qualities in domestic and franchise cricket, most recently leading Royal Challengers Bengaluru to the Women's Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026. Having been part of the Indian team since 2013, Smriti brings considerable experience into the role. She will now take on the responsibility of leading the side, with the team entering a new phase and continuing to build on the progress made in recent years. While she will be the full-time white-ball captain from now on, Smriti has led India in 18 T20Is and 4 ODIs. Speaking on her appointment, Smriti Mandhana said: “To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour. Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply. I am grateful to the BCCI, the selectors, my teammates and everyone who has supported me throughout my journey and for the trust they have placed in me. "I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey. "I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian Cricket forward.” Mr Mithun Manhas, BCCI President, said:“I congratulate Smriti on being entrusted with the responsibility of leading the Indian Women’s Cricket Team. She has been an important part of Indian cricket for many years and has consistently shown the qualities required to lead from the front. Her experience and understanding of the game will be valuable as she takes on this responsibility. “The BCCI has full confidence in Smriti and I am sure she will approach this role with the same commitment and professionalism that she has shown throughout her career. On behalf of the BCCI, I wish her the very best and look forward to seeing her lead the team into this new chapter.” Mr Devajit Saikia, BCCI Honorary Secretary, said: “Congratulations to Smriti on this important responsibility. She has grown into one of the most experienced players in the Indian team and has been part of some very important moments in the journey of Indian women’s cricket. She understands what it means to represent India and I am confident that she will bring that understanding to her role as captain. “Leading India is a significant responsibility, but Smriti has the experience and temperament to take it on. Her success as captain of Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the Women’s Premier League is another example of her leadership qualities. I wish her and the team every success in the journey ahead and look forward to seeing Indian Cricket continue to progress under her leadership.” BCCI

articles.pageText: BCCI invites applications for one position on the Men’s Selection Committee Press Releases BCCI invites applications for one position on the Men’s Selection Committee Share 5d ago MEDIA ADVISORY October 6, 2026 BCCI invites applications for one position on the Men’s Selection Committee The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) invites applications for one position on its Men’s Selection Committee. The member of the Men’s Selection Committee will be responsible for selecting the Senior National Men’s Team for representation in Tests, One Day Internationals, Twenty20 Internationals and any other format. The Committee will also play an important role in identifying talent and developing a strong bench strength for the Senior National Men’s Team. Key Responsibilities The member of the Men’s Selection Committee will be responsible for: Selecting the best possible Senior National Men’s Team in a fair and transparent manner, while identifying talent and developing a strong bench strength. Scouting and assessing players through domestic and international matches and contributing to the selection and development of the Senior National Men’s Team across formats. Attending team meetings and travelling to watch domestic and international matches, as required. Preparing and providing quarterly evaluation reports on the team’s performance to the Apex Council of BCCI. Addressing the media on team selection. Appointing the captain for the team in each format. Qualifications & Experience Should have played a minimum of 7 Test Matches; OR 30 First-Class Matches; OR 10 One Day International Matches and 20 First-Class Matches. Must have retired from the game at least five years previously. Any person who has been a member of any Cricket Committee, as defined in the Memorandum of Association and Rules and Regulations of the BCCI, for a cumulative period of five years will not be eligible to be a member of the Men’s Selection Committee. Application Details Number of Positions: 1 (One) Eligible candidates may submit their applications by5:00 PM IST on October 14, 2026through the link below: LINK TO APPLY CLICK HEREfor details After the screening and shortlisting process, shortlisted candidates will be called for personal interviews for further evaluation. BCCI

articles.title: BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket
articles.pageTitle: BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket
articles.description: MEDIA ADVISORY October 6, 2026 BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCC
articles.pageText: BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket Press Releases BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket Share 5d ago MEDIA ADVISORY October 6, 2026 BCCI acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur's leadership and contribution to Indian Cricket The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) acknowledges Harmanpreet Kaur’s contribution as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats. Harmanpreet has stepped down from the captaincy, bringing to a close a significant chapter of her leadership journey. Over the years, she has been a central figure in the growth of Indian women's cricket, leading the team through some of the most significant moments in its journey. Harmanpreet's leadership journey began unexpectedly in 2012. With Mithali Raj and Jhulan Goswami ruled out of the Women's T20 Asia Cup final through injury, the responsibility of leading India fell on a young Harmanpreet. She embraced the opportunity and led India to an 18-run victory over Pakistan, helping the team win the inaugural Women's T20 Asia Cup. It was her first experience of leading India and the beginning of a leadership journey that would span more than a decade. In 2016, Harmanpreet became India's regular T20I captain and, following Mithali Raj's retirement from international cricket, took over the ODI and Test captaincy in 2022. Her tenure as captain coincided with a period of significant growth for Indian women's cricket, with the team gaining depth and experience and becoming increasingly competitive across formats. India reached major finals, competed consistently against the strongest teams in the world and developed the belief to take on the biggest challenges. There were setbacks along the way, but each campaign added to a team that was becoming more accustomed to playing under pressure and expecting to compete for the biggest prizes in the game. Harmanpreet was one of the central figures in that progress. Harmanpreet's own performances were often a reflection of that ambition. Long before she became India's all-format captain, her unbeaten 171 against Australia in the 2017 Women's Cricket World Cup semi-final produced one of the most memorable individual performances in women's cricket. With India in a difficult position, Harmanpreet took the game away from Australia with an innings of extraordinary power and authority, taking India into the World Cup final. But the impact of that innings went far beyond the result. It was a performance that captured the imagination of the country, showed that Indian women could produce match-winning performances of the highest order on the biggest stage and inspired a generation of young women cricketers to dream of producing such moments for India. As captain, she experienced the full range of international cricket. India reached the final of the 2020 Women's T20 World Cup, won silver at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and claimed its first Asian Games gold. In 2025, Harmanpreet became the first Indian women's captain to lift the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup, guiding India to its historic maiden title. She played a crucial role in the semi-final against Australia, scoring 89 and sharing a match-changing 167-run partnership with Jemimah Rodrigues as India chased down a record 339. India then defeated South Africa by 52 runs in the final in Navi Mumbai to create history. The World Cup triumph was the defining achievement of Harmanpreet's captaincy and one of the most significant moments in the history of Indian women's cricket. Her final assignment as captain provided another major milestone. In Nagoya, Harmanpreet led India to a second consecutive Asian Games gold medal, defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. Her tenure also coincided with remarkable longevity. This year, she became the most-capped international player in women's cricket, the first player to appear in 200 T20Is and the first to captain in 150 T20Is. In her communication to the BCCI,Harmanpreet said: “Leading India has been one of the greatest honours and privileges of my life. The responsibility of wearing the India jersey and, above all, having the opportunity to lead my country has given me some of the most cherished moments of my cricketing journey. I would like to sincerely thank the BCCI, the selectors, the coaching staff, support staff, my teammates, and everyone who has stood by me throughout my tenure as captain. I am deeply grateful for the trust and confidence that was placed in me and for the opportunities I have received to serve Indian cricket in this role. After careful consideration, I believe that this is the right time for me to hand over the responsibility of captaincy and allow the team to move forward under new leadership. However, my commitment to Indian cricket remains as strong as ever. I would like to continue representing the Indian Women’s Cricket Team as a player and contribute to the team’s success in every way I can. I remain fully committed to giving my best on the field and supporting the team, the new leadership and the younger players with the same passion and dedication. I look forward to continuing this journey in the India jersey and contributing to Indian cricket with the same pride, humility and commitment that I have always carried.” The BCCI thanks Harmanpreet Kaur for the responsibility with which she led India, the belief she brought to the team and the contribution she has made to Indian Cricket. Mr Mithun Manhas, BCCI President, said:“Harmanpreet Kaur's contribution as captain will always hold a special place in the history of Indian Cricket. She took on the responsibility at an important stage in the growth of women's cricket and helped the Indian team build on the strong foundation laid by those who came before her. Over the years, she led India through some very important moments and helped the team compete with confidence against the best in the world. "The World Cup victory in 2025 will undoubtedly be the defining achievement of her captaincy. It was the culmination of years of progress, hard work and belief. Her Asian Games gold medals and the many important victories during her tenure further underline the contribution she has made. On behalf of the BCCI, I thank Harmanpreet for her leadership and the responsibility she has shown throughout her tenure as captain. I am pleased that she will continue to represent India as a player. Her experience, understanding of the game and presence in the dressing room will remain valuable to the Indian team.” Mr Devajit Saikia, BCCI Honorary Secretary, said:“Harmanpreet, you can be immensely proud of what you have achieved as captain of India. You embraced the responsibility from the very beginning and went on to lead India through some of the most important moments in its journey, while playing an important role in the growth of Indian women's cricket. "You experienced the disappointment of falling short, but continued to believe in the team and its ability to achieve more. That is what made the World Cup victory in 2025 so special. You had been part of the journey for many years and eventually had the opportunity to lead India to its first Women's Cricket World Cup title. That will always remain one of the great moments in Indian Cricket. "I also appreciate the thought and consideration with which you have taken this decision. You have chosen to hand over the responsibility at a time when you believe the team is ready for a new chapter, while continuing to contribute as a player. Your experience and the example you set for the younger players will remain important to this team. Thank you for everything you have given Indian Cricket as captain, and I look forward to seeing you continue your journey in the India jersey.” BCCI

articles.pageText: BCCI announces Muthoot FinCorp as Title Sponsor for India Home Cricket Press Releases BCCI announces Muthoot FinCorp as Title Sponsor for India Home Cricket Share Sat 26 Sep 2026, 12:24 pm MEDIA ADVISORY September 26, 2026 BCCI announces Muthoot FinCorp as Title Sponsor for India Home Cricket The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announces Muthoot FinCorp Limited as the Title Sponsor for India Home Cricket, with the association running through March 2028. The title sponsorship will cover all international series and tournaments played in India as well as all domestic tournaments organised by the Board. The association brings together Muthoot FinCorp’s strong presence across India with the nationwide reach of Indian cricket. Muthoot FinCorp’s distinctive blue also creates a natural visual connect with the Men and Women in Blue of Indian cricket. The partnership will provide Muthoot FinCorp with an opportunity to connect with cricket audiences across the country through India’s national teams and key domestic competitions. The association will commence with India’s first ODI against the West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday. BCCI President Mr Mithun Manhas said: “Indian cricket’s home season brings together the national teams, domestic competitions and players at different stages of their journey. Muthoot FinCorp’s association as Title Sponsor reflects the strength and reach of Indian cricket and the connection it has with people across the country. “There is also a natural connect between the two brands, with Muthoot FinCorp’s distinctive blue coming together with the Men and Women in Blue of Indian cricket. We are pleased to welcome Muthoot FinCorp to the BCCI family and look forward to building a strong association over the coming seasons.” BCCI Honorary Secretary Mr Devajit Saikia said:“India’s home season represents the entire spectrum of our cricketing structure. From our senior national teams and India A to our age-group teams and domestic competitions, every part of this calendar has an important role to play in the development of Indian cricket. “It is particularly encouraging to see Muthoot FinCorp’s association extend across this broad platform. We are delighted to welcome them as Title Sponsor and look forward to working closely with the Muthoot Pappachan Group as we continue to provide opportunities for players and bring high-quality cricket to fans across the country.” BCCI Vice President Mr Rajeev Shukla said:“The strength of Indian cricket is built on a robust domestic structure, with competitions such as the Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy providing an important pathway for players aspiring to represent India. Having Muthoot FinCorp associated with this part of Indian cricket is a positive development. “This partnership will allow Muthoot FinCorp to be part of the journey of players at different stages, while also connecting with cricket audiences across the country. We welcome them to the BCCI family and look forward to a successful association.” BCCI Treasurer Mr A. Raghuram Bhat said:“The continued interest of leading brands in associating with BCCI cricket reflects the strength of Indian cricket and the reach it has across the country. A title sponsorship that spans international and domestic cricket also demonstrates the breadth of opportunities that Indian cricket offers its partners. “Muthoot FinCorp has built a strong presence across India, and its association with Indian cricket provides an opportunity to bring that reach together with the nationwide appeal of the sport. We are pleased to begin this partnership and look forward to a productive relationship in the seasons ahead.” BCCI Joint Secretary Mr Prabhtej Bhatia said:“Cricket is followed across India in many different ways, and the home season allows fans to stay connected with the game throughout the year. From international cricket to domestic competitions and the emergence of young players, there are stories that resonate with people across the country. “Muthoot FinCorp’s association will span teams, competitions and regions, giving the brand an opportunity to be part of that journey. We are delighted to welcome them on board and look forward to building a strong relationship in the years ahead.” Thomas George Muthoot, Joint Managing Director, Muthoot FinCorp Limited, said, “Cricket provides a meaningful way to connect with the Indian public. We believe our association with BCCI reflects our commitment to supporting Indian cricket across national and domestic platforms.” Shaji Varghese, Chief Executive Officer, Muthoot FinCorp Limited, said,“This association with BCCI includes India’s Senior Men’s National Team, Senior Women’s National Team, India A Men’s Team, India B Men’s Team, India A Women’s Team, Under-19 Men’s and Women’s Teams, and other designated teams. It also covers key domestic competitions, including the Ranji Trophy, Irani Cup, Duleep Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy, Deodhar Trophy and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. This gives us an opportunity to be part of everyday Indian’s story.” BCCI

articles.description: Team India Women created history at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan by securing back-to-back gold medals in the women’s cricket competition. The triumphant Wom
articles.pageText: History in Nagoya: Women in Blue bag Team India's First Gold Medal at Asian Games 2026 Match Reports History in Nagoya: Women in Blue bag Team India's First Gold Medal at Asian Games 2026 Share Mon 21 Sep 2026, 10:00 pm Team India Women created history at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan by securing back-to-back gold medals in the women’s cricket competition. The triumphant Women in Blue made everyone proud by bagging the nation’s first Gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games. After winning the gold medal at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2022, the Harmanpreet Kaur-led side successfully defended the title with a dominating display on the field. View X post India started their Asian Games 2026 campaign with a clinical 8-wicket win against Japan in the quarter-final. After opting to bowl first, India reduced Japan to 57 in the first innings and chased down the target inside the powerplay. Sree Charani claimed a four-wicket haul and Shafali Verma wrapped the chase in style, scoring an unbeaten 40 off just 15 deliveries. View Instagram post In the semi-final fixture against Bangladesh, it was Shafali Verma once again with an exemplary knock that powered India to the Final. The Team India opener smashed her maiden T20I century off just 49 deliveries and guided India to 195/4 in the first innings. India cruised to the final after Bangladesh were all out for just 81, courtesy of three-wicket hauls from Nandni Sharma and Deepti Sharma. India met Sri Lanka in the summit clash, in the Gold medal event of the competition. After electing to bat first, India repeated the heroics of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 Final by putting a formidable performance with the bat against the same finalists. Vice-captain Smriti Mandhana scored a spectacular 79 off just 45 deliveries and put India in a commanding position against Sri Lanka in the final. Smriti Mandhana also became the first batter to reach the landmark of 11,000 international runs in women’s cricket as Team India set a mighty target of 217 for Sri Lanka. The spinners carried India’s momentum forward and put on a skilful economical show with the ball as Sri Lanka were all out for 69. India secured Gold medal with a comprehensive 147-run win. Opener Shafali Verma became the leading run-getter of the tournament, scoring 188 runs in three innings while Sree Charani topped the wicket-taking charts, scalping 8 wickets in three matches.

articles.pageTitle: India complete 3-0 Friendship Cup sweep as Abhishek Sharma rewrites record books
articles.description: India wrapped up the Friendship Cup with a commanding 127-run victory over Afghanistan in the third and final T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on T
articles.pageText: India complete 3-0 Friendship Cup sweep as Abhishek Sharma rewrites record books Match Reports India complete 3-0 Friendship Cup sweep as Abhishek Sharma rewrites record books Share Fri 18 Sep 2026, 3:15 pm India wrapped up the Friendship Cup with a commanding 127-run victory over Afghanistan in the third and final T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on Thursday, completing a 3-0 series sweep. The night belonged to opener Abhishek Sharma, who produced a record-breaking innings that rewrote the T20I record books. The left-hander raced to his century in just 30 deliveries — the fastest T20I hundred by a batter from a Full Member nation, surpassing the previous record jointly held by Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza and New Zealand's Finn Allen by three balls. It was also the fastest century by an Indian, comfortably eclipsing Rohit Sharma's 35-ball effort against Sri Lanka in 2017. View Instagram post Abhishek's assault began from the very first over. He took 16 balls to reach his fifty before adding the next fifty runs in just 14 more deliveries. He finished with 108 off 34 balls, an innings that included nine fours and 11 sixes, striking at 317.65. Sanju Samson provided excellent support with a second successive half-century, making 50 off 35 balls as the opening pair added 142 runs in just 9.5 overs. India raced to 100 in the powerplay — the team's highest-ever powerplay score in T20Is. View Instagram post Afghanistan's chase never gathered any momentum. After a promising start of 31 without loss, the innings unravelled dramatically. Axar Patel struck twice in the powerplay to remove Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal, before Jasprit Bumrah and Yash Thakur chipped in with wickets. Nitish Kumar Reddy then delivered the decisive blow, claiming three wickets in a single over — including the prized scalps of Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman — to snuff out any hopes of a fightback. Ravi Bishnoi cleaned up the tail with 3 for 26 as Afghanistan were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs. The first two matches followed remarkably similar patterns, with India chasing down modest targets with consummate ease. In the series opener on September 13, Afghanistan were reduced to 43 for 5 after seven overs before Azmatullah Omarzai's unbeaten 64 off 44 balls lifted them to 156 for 8. Arshdeep Singh was the pick of the bowlers with 3 for 19, while Jasprit Bumrah marked his return to T20I cricket with a disciplined spell. Abhishek Sharma then made light work of the chase, smashing 82 off 32 balls with seven fours and seven sixes, sharing a 121-run stand with Ishan Kishan (42) as India romped home in 13.4 overs. The second T20I on September 15 was even more one-sided. Afghanistan managed 159 for 8, with captain Ibrahim Zadran's 37 off 33 the only innings of substance. Nitish Kumar Reddy continued his impressive series with 3 for 24, while Axar Patel claimed 2 for 9. India's response was brutal. Sanju Samson, after a first-ball duck in the opener, struck a blistering 57 off just 22 balls, while Abhishek contributed 39 off 19. The opening pair added 88 in just 6.2 overs as India chased down the target in 14.5 overs with seven wickets to spare. View Instagram post A sporting finale The evening ended on a note that embodied the spirit of the Friendship Cup. During the trophy presentation, India captain Shreyas Iyer called Afghanistan skipper Ibrahim Zadran onto the podium, inviting him to share the silverware and join the Indian team for the traditional winners' photograph. The gesture evoked memories of 2018, when stand-in captain Ajinkya Rahane invited the Afghanistan squad to join India's victory photograph after Afghanistan's historic maiden Test in Bengaluru, handing over the trophy to the debutants in a poignant display of sportsmanship. Abhishek Sharma was named both Player of the Match for the final game and Player of the Series, finishing with 229 runs across the three matches at an average of 76.33 and a strike rate of 269.41. Nitish Kumar Reddy ended as the series' leading wicket-taker with six scalps. View X post India will now travel to Japan for a historic one-off T20I against the host nation on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground, a fixture that marks the first-ever meeting between the two sides in men's international cricket and launches the celebrations marking the 75th anniversary of India-Japan diplomatic relations. The match will also serve as preparation ahead of the Asian Games, where India enter at the quarterfinal stage, with their opening match scheduled for September 28.

The key decisions made are as under: The following 2 (two) representatives of the General Body were elected and inducted in the Governing Council of the IPL: (a) Mr. Arun Singh Dhumal; and (b) Mr. M Khairul Jamal Majumdar. The new Internal Committee of BCCI was formed under the BCCI’s Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policy. The BCCI Age Verification Policy was updated and adopted. articles.pageTitle: Abhishek Sharma breaks records galore with superb 30-ball hundred vs AFG
articles.description: It was a record-breaking night for Team India opening batter Abhishek Sharma during the third and final T20I between Afghanistan and India in the Friendship Cup
articles.pageText: Abhishek Sharma breaks records galore with superb 30-ball hundred vs AFG Features & Interviews Abhishek Sharma breaks records galore with superb 30-ball hundred vs AFG Share Fri 18 Sep 2026, 10:15 am It was a record-breaking night for Team India opening batter Abhishek Sharma during the third and final T20I between Afghanistan and India in the Friendship Cup 2026 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. Abhishek’s jaw-dropping innings of 108(34) that included nine fours and 11 sixes saw him scale new heights in his T20I career. Abhishek went into the third T20I already in fine form, having scored 121 runs in the first two matches, including a 32-ball 82 in the first T20I on September 13. The 26-year-old southpaw from Punjab thus ended the series with 229 runs from 3 matches, with an average of 76.33 and a strike-rate of 269.41, including 22 sixes throughout the series. He bagged the Player of the Series award to go along with the Player of the Match award for his scintillating century in the third T20I. View Instagram post Here’s a look at the key records broken by Abhishek during his knock of 108(34): Abhishek Sharma’s century, scored in just 30 balls, is the fastest by an Indian batter in T20Is. He broke the previous record held by former Team India Captain Rohit Sharma, who scored a 35-ball hundred against Sri Lanka at the Holkar Cricket Stadium, Indore, on 22 December 2017. Abhishek’s 30-ball ton is the fastest century by a batter against a Test playing nation in T20Is. It is also the third fastest hundred overall in T20 Internationals, behind Sahil Chauhan’s 27-ball ton for Estonia against Cyprus in 2024, and Muhammad Fahad’s 29-ball hundred for Turkey against Bulgaria in 2025. Abhishek now holds the first and second positions on the list of most sixes hit in a T20I innings for India. His 11 sixes against Afghanistan on Thursday sit just behind his 13 sixes against England in Mumbai in February last year. View Instagram post

articles.description: The Women in Blue secured the ACC Women’s Asia Cup title for the record eighth time after registering a clinical 72-run victory against defending champions Sri
articles.pageText: India clinch Women's Asia Cup Title for the record eighth time Match Reports India clinch Women's Asia Cup Title for the record eighth time Share Wed 16 Sep 2026, 11:30 am The Women in Blue secured the ACC Women’s Asia Cup title for the record eighth time after registering a clinical 72-run victory against defending champions Sri Lanka at the Dubai International Stadium, in Dubai. Team India had an invincible run by remaining unbeaten throughout the tournament. View Instagram post Team India’s campaign began with a commanding 94-run win over Thailand. Opener Shafali Verma started the tournament on a positive note after scoring 64 off just 36 deliveries in the first innings. An impressive bowling display, led by three-wicket hauls from Deepti Sharma and Nandni Sharma helped India defend the target with ease. India’s second game of the league stage saw vice-captain Smriti Mandhana break an all-time record as she surpassed the legendary former India Captain Mithali Raj in the list of most runs in international women’s cricket. The Team India vice-captain scored a scintillating ton against Hong Kong as India registered a massive 137-run victory. View X post The domination continued for India in the league stage after a comprehensive seven-wicket win over Pakistan with more than 11 overs to spare. Sree Charani and Prema Rawat spun the web and claimed three wickets each as Pakistan were all out for just 55. India’s match against Pakistan was a memorable game for Captain Harmanpreet Kaur, who became the first captain in the world, across both men’s and women’s cricket to play 150 matches as a captain. India completed a 40-run win over Bangladesh in the semi-final. Opener Shafali Verma once again put on a show with the bat, scoring an entertaining 64 off just 40 deliveries. Deepti Sharma’s three wicket haul in the second innings later helped India restrict Bangladesh to 109/7. India faced defending champions Sri Lanka in the final, a repeat fixture of the 2024 edition. It was the Smriti-Shafali show in the final as the openers put together a spectacular 129-run partnership and powered India to a massive total of 183/5 in the first innings. A disciplined bowling performance, led by Sree Charani (4/20) and Deepti Sharma (3/19) ensured India’s comfortable victory at the end, securing India’s eighth Women’s Asia Cup title.

articles.pageText: BCCI invites applications for the position of Head – Sports Science & Medicine at the Centre of Excellence Press Releases BCCI invites applications for the position of Head – Sports Science & Medicine at the Centre of Excellence Share Fri 11 Sep 2026, 10:50 am MEDIA ADVISORY September 11, 2026 BCCI invites applications for the position of Head – Sports Science & Medicine at the Centre of Excellence The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) invites applications for the position of Head – Sports Science and Medicine at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE), Bengaluru. The successful candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership to BCCI’s Sports Science and Medicine services across its elite cricket and CoE programmes. The role will also involve line management of the Head of Physiotherapy (CoE), Team India Head of Physiotherapy, Head S&C (CoE) and Team India S&C, while working closely with National and CoE coaches, Cricket Education and other performance specialists to deliver integrated support programmes for Indian players. The position will have a key focus on player welfare, injury prevention and rehabilitation, physical development, research, innovation and the adoption of relevant technologies and services. Key Responsibilities The Head – Sports Science and Medicine will: Develop and implement the strategic vision, objectives and framework for BCCI’s Sports Science and Medicine department, including clinical and medical governance, service delivery, risk management and player welfare. Provide strategic and operational leadership to the Sports Science and Medicine team and work closely with the Head Cricket – CoE, National Coaches, Cricket Education and other performance specialists to deliver integrated support programmes for Indian players. Oversee programmes related to injury prevention and risk reduction, player recovery and rehabilitation, athlete development, illness and wellness management, and long-term physical development. Drive performance benchmarking, quality management, research and innovation, including the development of the department’s research wing and partnerships with leading sports and medical institutions. Oversee departmental planning, budgeting, performance management and professional development, while ensuring high standards of service delivery across BCCI programmes. Serve as a spokesperson on performance-related matters, as required. Qualifications & Experience Master’s degree in Sports Science or a closely related discipline; a Doctorate is preferred. Minimum five years’ experience in a strategic leadership role managing multidisciplinary performance teams. Extensive experience in developing and implementing strategic plans and delivering Sports Science or Medicine support to high-performance teams in professional and/or Olympic sport. Current professional accreditation/licence in a Sports Science or Medicine discipline. Experience in performance-focused research and an understanding of the long-term physical development of players. Experience of working with regional performance and sports institutes is desirable. Previous experience as a Chief Medical Officer or Medical Director, specialist recognition in Sport & Exercise Medicine, and experience in medical and clinical governance will be considered desirable. Employment Details Position:Head – Sports Science and Medicine Location:BCCI Centre of Excellence, Bengaluru Number of Openings:1 Age Limit:Below 60 years Reports to:Head of Cricket – Centre of Excellence, Bengaluru Application Details Interested candidates are required to submit their applicationsHEREby5:00 PM on 30th September. The detailed Job Description can be accessedHERE. Following the screening and shortlisting of applications, shortlisted candidates may be called for personal interviews for further evaluation. BCCI

articles.pageText: BCCI announces Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT as Associate Partners for India Home Cricket Press Releases BCCI announces Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT as Associate Partners for India Home Cricket Share Tue 8 Sep 2026, 2:10 pm MEDIA ADVISORY September 8, 2026 BCCI announces Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT as Associate Partners for India Home Cricket The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announces the appointment of Campa,SBI Life and ChatGPT as Associate Partners for India Home Cricket for a two-season period, commencing with India’s upcoming home series against the West Indies and running through March 2028. The three new partnerships have a combined deal value of over ₹130 crore, representing a 44% increase over the previous cycle, underscoring the strong appeal and growing commercial value of India’s home cricket season. The partnerships further broaden the BCCI’s commercial portfolio, bringing together leading brands across the beverage, insurance and AI technology sectors and creating new opportunities to connect with cricket fans. They reflect the versatility of Indian cricket as a platform for businesses to build visibility, reach consumers and engage with a large and passionate fan base. Commenting on the announcement,BCCI President, Mr Mithun Manhas, said:“India’s home season continues to be a valuable and sought-after sporting property in the country, and the signing of Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT is a strong endorsement of the strength of the Indian cricket ecosystem. The big increase in the combined value of these partnerships is particularly encouraging. It reflects the trust that leading brands have in the reach, engagement and commercial potential that comes with being associated with BCCI. “Each brings a distinct brand and proposition to Indian cricket, and we look forward to working with them to build strong associations that create greater value for all stakeholders.” BCCI Honorary Secretary, Mr Devajit Saikia, said:“The significant growth in the value of our home season partnerships reflects the strength of the property and the confidence that brands have in the BCCI and Team India. A 44% increase in the combined deal value, with the latest partnerships valued at over ₹130 crore, is a significant achievement and demonstrates the strong demand for association with Indian cricket. “Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT represent three very different and exciting categories, and their association highlights the diverse opportunities that our home season offers. We are pleased to welcome them as Associate Partners and look forward to working with them to create new ways to engage with fans and enhance their experience of Indian cricket.” About the partners Campa:Campa is an iconic Indian beverage brand, with a rich legacy and a strong connection with generations of consumers. Today, Campa has evolved into a total beverage brand with a strong presence across multiple categories, combining its distinctive Indian heritage with a bold, contemporary spirit. With a portfolio built for the tastes and aspirations of today’s consumers, Campa represents the resurgence of a proudly Indian brand with scale, relevance and ambition. SBI Life:SBI Life Insurance is India’s leading life insurance company, with a strong legacy of trust and a commitment to helping individuals and families build a financially secure future. The brand has consistently focused on empowering people to protect what matters most and pursue their aspirations with greater confidence. ChatGPT:ChatGPT is OpenAI’s AI-powered conversational assistant that understands and responds to people in natural, human-like language. It can generate text, speech, and images in response to user prompts. BCCI

articles.pageText: India to play Japan in historic T20I in Sano BCCI News India to play Japan in historic T20I in Sano Share Fri 4 Sep 2026, 11:00 am The Japan Cricket Association (JCA) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) are delighted to announce that the men’s teams from each nation will play a T20 International match to launch the celebrations of the 75th anniversary of India-Japan Diplomatic Relations. The Suzuki Cup will take place at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture on Tuesday, 22nd September 2026. The match will be the first step of “Sport 75”, an initiative that stems from an agreement reached during a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Indian Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and aims to promote human exchanges and cooperation between India and Japan in the field of sports, taking note of India’s ambition to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games in 2036. BCCI Honorary Secretary, Mr Devajit Saikia, said:“The BCCI is delighted to be part of this historic occasion as the Indian and Japanese men’s teams come together for a special T20 International in Japan. This is a significant moment for cricket, as it takes the Indian team to new territory and provides an opportunity to introduce the sport to a wider audience in Japan and East Asia. “India and Japan share a strong and longstanding relationship and friendship, and we are pleased that cricket will be part of the celebrations marking 75 years of bilateral relations between the two countries, and we thank the Japan Cricket Association (JCA) for its efforts in making this fixture possible. “The BCCI believes that the growth of cricket must extend beyond its traditional territories, and as the world’s largest cricket board, we recognise our responsibility to contribute to that growth. “The BCCI will work closely with the JCA to further strengthen cricket in Japan and to build on this relationship in the years ahead.” JCA CEO Naoki Miyaji said:“To be able to invite the reigning World Champions to then home of cricket in Japan is a landmark moment for our association. We thank the BCCI for working with us towards this goal and greatly look forward to welcoming the passion of Indian cricket fans, and we actively encourage any local Japanese people curious about cricket to come and cheer on our team in what will be a truly memorable occasion.” BCCI

articles.pageText: India to host inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 Press Releases India to host inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 Share Wed 2 Sep 2026, 1:30 pm The International Cricket Council (ICC) today announced that the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 will be staged in the Indian cities of Mumbai and Vadodara from 14 to 28 February. The Cricket Club of India (CCI) in Mumbai and the Vadodara International Cricket Stadium will be the venues for the landmark tournament that will bring together six of the world’s leading women’s cricket teams - Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka. Those six teams, who qualified as per their positions in the ICC Women’s T20I Team Rankings on the 6 July qualification cut-off date, will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on 28 February. The tournament was originally scheduled to be held in Sri Lanka but will now be staged in India as Sri Lanka Cricket continues to make the requisite reforms outlined at the ICC’s Annual Conference in July. The ICC assessed three candidates - Bangladesh, India and South Africa - against its established host evaluation criteria before recommending India as the replacement host, a decision ratified by the ICC Board on 2 September. ICC Chairman, Mr. Jay Shah, said:“The ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket. As the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage. “With a marquee ICC women’s event now taking place every year, we have a significant opportunity to build greater momentum, provide more consistency and create a stronger rhythm for the women’s game, its players and its fans around the world.” Ticketing information and the full ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 schedule will follow in due course.

articles.pageText: BCCI invites applications for five positions on the Junior Cricket Committee Press Releases BCCI invites applications for five positions on the Junior Cricket Committee Share Mon 24 Aug 2026, 7:00 am MEDIA ADVISORY August 24, 2026 BCCI invites applications for five positions on the Junior Cricket Committee The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) invites applications for five positions on its Junior Cricket Committee. The members of the Junior Cricket Committee will be responsible for selecting age-group teams up to Under-22 for coaching camps and for India’s junior fixtures against domestic and international opposition, both in India and overseas, across formats. The committee will also play an important role in developing a strong talent pool and bench strength for India’s junior teams. Key Responsibilities Members of the Junior Cricket Committee will be responsible for: Selecting the best possible age-group teams up to Under-22 in a fair and transparent manner, while identifying talent and developing a strong bench strength for India’s junior teams. Scouting and assessing players through domestic and international matches and contributing to the selection and development of teams for coaching camps, tours and tournaments in India and overseas. Vetting and selecting coaches and support staff for the respective teams, including physiotherapists, trainers, therapists, analysts and medics. Overseeing the performance and development of junior teams, including preparing periodic evaluation reports and appointing captains across formats. Organising and conducting BCCI junior tournaments and overseas junior tours, while addressing matters relating to the conduct and administration of junior tournaments. Promoting strong ethical values among young cricketers, including awareness around issues such as drugs, betting and match-fixing, through interactions with senior and former players. Qualifications & Experience Former players who have played a minimum of 25 First-Class matches. Must have retired from the game at least five years previously. Any person who has been a member of any Cricket Committee, as defined in the Memorandum of Association and Rules and Regulations of the BCCI, for a cumulative period of five years will not be eligible to be a member of the Junior Cricket Committee. Application Details Number of Positions: 5 (Five) Eligible candidates may submit their applications by5:00 PM IST on September 5, 2026through the link below: LINK TO APPLY After the screening and shortlisting process, shortlisted candidates will be called for personal interviews for further evaluation. articles.pageText: Afghanistan to host India for three-match T20I series in Delhi Press Releases Afghanistan to host India for three-match T20I series in Delhi Share Wed 12 Aug 2026, 5:25 am Summary The Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) have confirmed that Afghanistan will host India for a three-match T20I series at the Arun Jaitley Cricket Stadium in Delhi from September 13 to 17, 2026. The series will get underway on September 13, with the second T20I scheduled for September 15 and the third on September 17. All three matches will be played at the same venue. The series is part of Afghanistan's Future Tours Program and will be played in India, where Afghanistan has hosted its home fixtures in recent years. Afghanistan to host India for three-match T20I series in Delhi The Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) have confirmed that Afghanistan will host India for a three-match T20I series at the Arun Jaitley Cricket Stadium in Delhi from September 13 to 17, 2026. The series will get underway on September 13, with the second T20I scheduled for September 15 and the third on September 17. All three matches will be played at the same venue. The series is part of Afghanistan's Future Tours Program and will be played in India, where Afghanistan has hosted its home fixtures in recent years. Speaking on the series, Mr Mithun Manhas, President, BCCI, said: “The BCCI remains committed to supporting the growth of cricket in Afghanistan and providing its players with opportunities to compete at the highest level. Bilateral cricket is an important part of this, as it allows teams to play regularly against quality opposition and gain valuable experience. We welcome the Afghanistan Cricket Board to India for this series and look forward to working closely with them to make it a successful one. We believe there is scope to do more together and will continue to support Afghanistan cricket while strengthening the relationship between the two cricketing nations.” Mr Devajit Saikia, Honorary Secretary, BCCI, said: “The BCCI is pleased to support the Afghanistan Cricket Board in hosting this T20I series in India. The India-Afghanistan cricketing rivalry has produced some thrilling encounters over the years, with both teams boasting quality cricketers. Afghanistan’s players are also quite popular among fans in India, which is a reflection of the strong bond that has developed between the two cricketing nations. India hosting Afghanistan for their historic first Test in 2018 was another significant milestone in this journey, and since then, we have continued to see regular bilateral engagements between the two teams. “We recently hosted Afghanistan for a Test and ODI series in June, and this T20I series will mean the two teams have now competed against each other across all three formats. We look forward to welcoming the Afghanistan team to Delhi and are confident that this will be an exciting and memorable series.” Mr Rohan Jaitley, President, DDCA, said: “We are delighted to welcome both teams to the Arun Jaitley Stadium for what promises to be an exciting T20I series. We look forward to hosting the teams and providing them with the best possible facilities and a memorable experience. I am confident that the three matches will give fans in Delhi an opportunity to enjoy some exciting cricket and further add to the rich history of international cricket at this iconic venue.” The upcoming series will add another chapter to the growing cricketing relationship between the two nations. Afghanistan most recently toured India for a three-match ODI series in June 2026, while the two sides also played a three-match T20I series in January 2024. India hosted Afghanistan for their historic first Test in 2018, and the two teams have since continued to engage regularly across formats. articles.description: The BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru is designed to bring together the different elements of elite performance — from cricket coaching and sports sc
articles.pageText: How the BCCI Centre of Excellence is shaping India's high-performance system Features & Interviews How the BCCI Centre of Excellence is shaping India's high-performance system Share Tue 11 Aug 2026, 8:50 am The BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru is designed to bring together the different elements of elite performance — from cricket coaching and sports science to sports medicine, strength and conditioning and technology. During a media interaction at the CoE, BCCI Head of Cricket VVS Laxman and Honorary Secretary Devajit Saikia spoke at length about the processes followed in managing player injuries, monitoring workloads and maintaining fitness across the Indian cricket pathway. Addressing questions around injuries and rehabilitation, Mr Laxman said the CoE's work begins with understanding the nature of an injury and continues until the player is ready to return to competitive cricket. "The process starts with diagnosing the injury and finishes with a player being declared fit after the two RTP matches we have," Mr Laxman said. Depending on the nature of the injury, the initial assessment may involve the Indian team's medical staff and specialist consultation. Once the diagnosis is established and the player reports to the CoE, the rehabilitation programme moves through different phases, starting with medical and physiotherapy intervention before progressing to strength and conditioning, cricket-specific skills and a gradual increase in workload. "And then we build up the load. And then we play two RTP matches before we declare the player fit," Mr Laxman said. The return-to-play process is benchmark-driven, with the CoE using data to assess whether a player has reached the required physical and skill levels before being cleared. "Until and unless the benchmark is met, or in fact got better, we don't release. So that's the benchmark we use to declare a player fit," he said. The objective, Mr Laxman added, is to ensure that when a player returns to the Indian team or competitive cricket, he or she is ready to perform from the outset. "From the first match, he has been able to perform to the best of his potential." However, he stressed that rehabilitation timelines cannot always be fixed. "It's a human body. It is not a machine where the timelines will always be met. So there's a continuous process of understanding how a player is progressing, and based on that, the load is increased." Monitoring players beyond the CoE Mr Laxman also addressed questions around players working with individual trainers and said there was a structured system in place to monitor players across the different levels of Indian cricket. The strength and conditioning staff with the Indian teams are responsible for centrally contracted players, while the CoE's S&C staff monitor targeted and age-group players. The information is captured through the Athlete Management System (AMS), with GPS technology also used to track player activity and workloads. "Everything is there on the AMS. Every session of the player is there on the AMS," Mr Laxman said. "Wherever the player is, whatever he's doing, it's documented." Mr Laxman said the Indian men's and women's teams have experienced strength and conditioning professionals working closely with the players and emphasised the importance of coordination and trust between the players and performance staff. "I think the trust and the coordination between the S&C and the players, as far as my knowledge is concerned, is going on." Technology has also helped the CoE monitor the workloads of fast bowlers, particularly when players are away from the facility. Mr Laxman said one of the key learnings from workload monitoring was that injuries are not necessarily caused by bowlers doing too much. In some cases, the risk can arise when bowlers are not sufficiently prepared for the demands placed on them. "Our learning is that stress injuries or injuries happen not because a fast bowler is bowling too much. It happens that the fast bowler is not bowling enough," he said. The CoE therefore sets an individual workload range for fast bowlers and monitors their bowling loads on a weekly basis. "There's a sweet spot we have for each and every fast bowler across the contracted, the targeted and the Under-19s, and there's a weekly monitoring of that load." ‘Injury is part and parcel of elite sport’ While acknowledging that modern players are required to play significantly more cricket than previous generations, Mr Laxman said injuries were an unavoidable part of elite sport. "There's no doubt that the modern generation of players has to play a lot more cricket than I used to play the game, obviously with the addition of T20 and the three formats," he said. "But when someone is playing at the elite level, you're supposed to give more than 100%. If you're not, then you're not doing justice to the role or for what purpose you're selected in the team." Mr Laxman said the focus should be on helping players understand their workloads, monitoring them effectively and continually improving systems rather than expecting injuries to be eliminated altogether. "Even though you do that, playing at the highest level, you can get injured. So if you're thinking about not getting injured, then you're not playing to the best of your ability." He added: "One thing which should be addressed is how you see injury. Do you see injury as a negative thing? Or do you think injury is part and parcel?" Monitoring becomes particularly important for players who have high physical demands, including allrounders. Mr Laxman cited Nitish Kumar Reddy's case while explaining the importance of helping players understand how to manage their workloads. "Being an all-rounder, obviously there is a lot of workload on him and how he becomes fitter — not only when he is playing various tournaments but also when he is not part of any tournaments." The CoE also conducts pre-season screening for contracted and targeted players, who undergo a series of fitness assessments and field-based tests. Mr Laxman highlighted the introduction of the Bronco Test, which can also be used during the season as part of a conditioning session. "While you are playing, it is very important for you to remain fit," he said. ‘Subject to fitness’ and seamless communication Mr Laxman also sought to clarify the process followed when players undergoing rehabilitation are named in squads subject to fitness clearance. He said there was close coordination between the CoE, team management, medical and sports science staff, the selectors and the BCCI. "We don't like to use the word blame because when you're using the name, then you're finding someone as a scapegoat," Mr Laxman said. "There's a brilliant coordination between the CoE, between the team management of both the teams and the SSM staff of both the teams and the selection committee." The CoE provides fitness status reports to the relevant selection committee, with copies also shared with the head coach and the BCCI. Mr Laxman explained that an asterisk next to a player's name in a BCCI squad announcement indicates that the player has been selected subject to fitness clearance. "When the media release comes from the BCCI, there's an asterisk attached to a player selection. And what does that asterisk mean? It means subject to fitness." The status can change depending on how a player progresses through rehabilitation. If the progression is slower than expected, the CoE communicates this to the selectors and team management. "Always it's player-centric and team-centric. So that communication is happening seamlessly," Mr Laxman said. Mr Saikia added that selection meetings are generally held three to four weeks before a team departs, which means a player undergoing rehabilitation may still have time to regain fitness before the series begins. "We do not outrightly reject him because on the date of selection, he is not fit," Mr Saikia said. "But by the time it will be effectively required for travel or to play the match, by that time he may be totally fit." That uncertainty is also why the final assessment has to be based on the player's progress rather than a fixed timetable. "As VVS has said, it is a human body. It is not a machine. He may take 14 days' time or he may take 28 days' time, subject to his own body composition." Search continues for the right specialist Mr Laxman and Mr Saikia also addressed the search for a replacement for the position previously held by Nitin Patel. Mr Laxman said the BCCI had undertaken an extensive interview process, but finding a candidate with the required experience and expertise remained important. "The lookout is there, but you have to find someone who is qualified and capable enough to take up that position," Mr Laxman said."We will quite definitely fill that position and the suitable candidate has to be identified." He said the BCCI was also looking to upskill existing personnel at the CoE while continuing the search for the right candidate. "The process is on. It is not that the BCCI is not looking for a suitable candidate, but you have to find the right candidate." Mr Saikia said finding someone with the required expertise was challenging because of the limited number of suitable professionals available. "There are very limited persons, not only in India but across the world," he said. "In spite of repeated processes being done, we are not getting the right candidate. But the process is on to find the right candidate." A culture of standards and continuous improvement Mr Laxman also spoke about the culture the CoE is seeking to create, pointing to players who set high standards through their approach and professionalism. "There is no doubt that Virat is an exemplary professional. The standards he sets for himself is something which he tries and meets each and every time he plays, whichever team," Mr Laxman said. "That's why he is a great role model. A lot of youngsters or players want to emulate him." For Mr Laxman, the success of a high-performance system is not measured solely by trophies but also by the processes it establishes and the players it helps develop. "Trophies are a by-product of what systems and processes you set," he said. "Those systems and processes are something which is in your control." He described the development of the new CoE as a significant milestone, particularly in providing players across different levels of the game with access to world-class infrastructure. "From April to September, the entire infrastructure of such a big scale is filled with players," he said, referring to the presence of players ranging from Under-15 and Under-16 cricketers to centrally contracted men's and women's players and other targeted players. "To see them work on their game, to see them get better each and every day, it can't be more meaningful than what I've experienced." Mr Saikia also addressed the issue of spectators at matches held at the CoE, explaining that restrictions attached to the use of the campus do not permit crowds at the venue. “There are some restrictions while this land was adopted here, it was said that we cannot have crowds here in the campus. So that is a government restriction and we cannot violate that. However, we’ve increased the number of matches being telecast live to give fans greater access to domestic cricket,” he added. The BCCI is also open to considering the possibility of hosting the final elsewhere if required. "We still have time. We'll look into that aspect." The discussions at the CoE underlined the complexity of managing elite cricketers in a calendar that spans international, domestic and franchise cricket. From diagnosis and rehabilitation to workload monitoring and return to play, the focus, Mr Laxman said, remains on helping players meet the demands of the game while ensuring that the systems supporting them continue to evolve.

articles.description: MEDIA ADVISORY July 30, 2026 BCCI pays tribute to Ajinkya Rahane's distinguished international career The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) congratul
articles.pageText: BCCI pays tribute to Ajinkya Rahane's distinguished international career Press Releases BCCI pays tribute to Ajinkya Rahane's distinguished international career Share Thu 30 Jul 2026, 9:30 am MEDIA ADVISORY July 30, 2026 BCCI pays tribute to Ajinkya Rahane's distinguished international career The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) congratulates Ajinkya Rahane on an outstanding international career following his decision to retire from international cricket. Over nearly a decade and a half, Rahane became one of India's most trusted performers. His calm presence, resilience and ability to deliver in the toughest situations earned him the respect of teammates, opponents and cricket lovers alike. At a time when India established itself as one of the strongest Test teams in the world, Rahane emerged as one of its most dependable batters, particularly in overseas conditions. Elegant at the crease and technically sound, he possessed the temperament to succeed when the conditions were at their most demanding. Time and again, when India found itself under pressure away from home, Rahane responded with innings of substance. His centuries at Lord's, Wellington, Melbourne, Kingston and Durban remain among the defining overseas hundreds by an Indian batter, each reflecting his ability to adapt, absorb pressure and rise to the occasion. His finest chapter came during the 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. Rahane took over the captaincy at a time when India was facing one of its toughest moments after being shot out for 36 in the pink-ball Test in Adelaide. With the squad navigating the challenges and restrictions brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic, expectations were firmly against India. He led from the front with a magnificent century at the MCG that levelled the series. What followed was one of the greatest triumphs in Indian Cricket. Under Rahane's calm leadership, India overcame injuries, inexperience and adversity to secure a memorable series victory, capped by the historic win at The Gabba, where Australia's 32-year unbeaten record came to an end. Leading India in six Test matches, Rahane remained unbeaten as captain, winning four and drawing two. His leadership was marked by clarity of thought, sound judgement, and the belief he instilled in those around him. As one of the senior members of the dressing room, he was respected for his humility, professionalism and willingness to put the team before himself. He led by example and earned the admiration of teammates, opponents and cricket fans through the way he carried himself both on and off the field. Across his international career, Rahane scored more than 8,000 runs. Yet, numbers alone cannot define his contribution. He brought assurance to the Indian team, calm in moments of pressure and led by example through his dedication to the game. The BCCI expresses its heartfelt gratitude to Ajinkya Rahane for his immense contribution to Indian Cricket. His professionalism, resilience and sportsmanship have left a lasting impact on the game and his journey will continue to inspire young cricketers across the country. Mr Mithun Manhas, BCCI President, said:"Ajinkya Rahane's career is a fine example of what it means to put the team first. He earned his reputation through performances in some of the toughest conditions in world cricket and became one of India's most dependable batters overseas. His leadership during the 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy will forever remain one of the defining chapters in Indian Cricket. Taking charge after the opening Test, he led a young side through extraordinary circumstances to a famous series victory, culminating in the historic triumph at The Gabba. On behalf of the BCCI, I congratulate Ajinkya on a distinguished international career and wish him every success in the years ahead." Mr Devajit Saikia, Honorary Secretary, BCCI, said:"Ajinkya, you can be immensely proud of the way you led India and the way you played this great game. You played cricket with the utmost sincerity and integrity, qualities every dressing room values. You let your cricket do the talking and earned the respect of everyone who shared a dressing room with you. Your contributions to Indian Cricket went far beyond the runs you scored. Through important innings, thoughtful leadership and the example you set for younger players, you made every team you represented stronger. I thank you for your outstanding service to Indian Cricket."

articles.pageText: BCCI announces the release of Request for Quotation for Associate Partner Rights for BCCI Events Press Releases BCCI announces the release of Request for Quotation for Associate Partner Rights for BCCI Events Share Mon 20 Jul 2026, 3:30 pm July 20, 2026 Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announces the release of Request for Quotation for Associate Partner Rights for BCCI Events. BCCI invites Quotations from reputed entities to acquire the Associate Partner Rights for BCCI Events, through a tender process. Accordingly, BCCI is issuing the Request for Quotation for Associate Partner Rights for BCCI Events (“RFQ”) which provides the detailed terms and conditions governing the submission and evaluation of Quotations. The RFQ will be made available on receipt of payment of a non-refundable fee ofINR 1,00,000 (Indian Rupees One Lakh Only) plus any applicable Goods and Services Tax. The Interested Parties may note the following timelines with respect to the RFQ: | Milestone | Date | Date of release of RFQ | July 20, 2026 | Last date to purchase the RFQ | August 14, 2026 | Last date to seek clarifications | August 16, 2026 | Date of submission of Quotation Documents | August 25, 2026 Interested parties are requested to email the details of payment made for the purchase of the RFQ torfq@bcci.tv, as per the procedure laid down inAnnexure A. It is clarified that the RFQ documents shall be shared only upon the confirmation of payment of the non-refundable RFQ fee. Any interested party wishing to submit a Quotation is required to purchase the RFQ. However, only those satisfying the eligibility criteria set out in the RFQ, and as laid down inAnnexure B, and subject to the other terms and conditions set out therein, shall be eligible to submit a Quotation. It is clarified that merely purchasing the RFQ does not entitle any person to submit a Quotation. BCCI reserves the right to cancel or amend the RFQ process at any stage in any manner without providing any reason. DEVAJIT SAIKIA Honorary Secretary BCCI ANNEXURE A PROCEDURE TO PROCURE THE RFQ DOCUMENTS The RFQ document can be purchased by anIndian entityas per the following procedure: If the purchasing entity is anIndian entity: Payment of INR 1,00,000 + 18,000 (GST) i.e.,Total INR 1,18,000(Indian Rupees One Lakh Eighteen Thousand Only) is to be made to the following bank account: INR Bank Account Details: Account Name: The Board of Control for Cricket in India Account No.: 60082778272 Name of the Bank: Bank of Maharashtra Branch: Fort Branch, Mumbai IFSC code: MAHB0000002 If the purchasing entity is aforeign entity: Payment of USD 1,050/- (USD One Thousand Fifty Only) is to be made to the following bank account: USD Bank Account Details: | Beneficiary Bank: | Bank of Maharashtra, | | Overseas Branch | | Mumbai | | Swift Code: MAHBINBBOVM | | Account No.: 60081674478 | | Account Name: The Board of Control for Cricket in India | Correspondent Bank: | Bank of New York, New York. | | Routing No.: 021 000 018 | | Swift Code: IRVTUS3N | | Account No.: 803-3165-537 Once the payment is made, the payment confirmation is required to be shared by email torfq@bcci.tvwith the subject line “Confirmation of Payment of RFQ Fee forAssociate Partner Rights” along with the following details: Name of the Party: Registered Address: Pan No (if applicable): GST No (if applicable): It is clarified that the RFQ documents shall be shared only upon receiving the payment and the details as mentioned above. It is further clarified that the RFQ must be purchased by the entity that is desiring to submit a Quotation. ANNEXURE B ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA The Interested Parties must note the following eligibility requirements with respect to the RFQ: 1.General Eligibility:Any entity registered in India. It is expressly clarified, for the avoidance of any doubt, that no quotations from any individual, unincorporated entity, consortia, joint ventures or joint bidders, will be accepted or considered for the purpose of this RFQ. 2.Financial Eligibility:The Interested Party shall fulfil either of the following requirements: The average audited annual Turnover of each Interested Party for the last 3 (three) years must be at leastINR 100,00,00,000(Indian Rupees One Hundred Crore only). Or The average Net Worth of each Interested Party for the last 3 (three) years must be at leastINR 100,00,00,000(Indian Rupees One Hundred Crore only), as per the last 3 (three) audited accounts. “Turnover” shall mean annual audited turnover of the Interested Party together, if necessary, with turnover from any company(ies) in the same Group as the Interested Party which may be consolidated with or otherwise added to the Interested Party’s turnover for the purposes of satisfying this threshold. “Net Worth” shall mean the aggregate value of the paid-up share capital of the Interested Party and all reserves created out of the profits, securities premium account and debit or credit balance of profit and loss account, after deducting the aggregate value of the accumulated losses, deferred expenditure and miscellaneous expenditure not written off, as per the audited balance sheet, but does not include reserves created out of revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation and amalgamation. For calculating the Net Worth, the net worth of any company(ies) in the same Group as the Interested Party can be consolidated with or otherwise added to the Interested Party’s Net Worth for the purposes of satisfying this threshold. 3.Fit and Proper Person:Each Interested Party must be a ‘Fit and Proper Person’. In order to determine whether a Person is a Fit and Proper Person, the BCCI may take into account any factor, as may be deemed fit by the BCCI, including without limitation any one or more of the following criteria: (i) not having been convicted by a court of a criminal offence or offences involving moral turpitude, economic offence or fraud; (ii) not having any conflict of interest as per the BCCI Conflict of Interest Rules; (iii) absence of conviction for any offence punishable with imprisonment for 2 (two) years or more in any jurisdiction; (iv) absence of categorisation as a wilful defaulter by the Reserve Bank of India; and/or (v) a Person having integrity and reputation; and the BCCI reserves the right to reject any quotation from any Interested Party which in the BCCI’s opinion and at its sole and absolute discretion does not satisfy this criteria. 4.Ineligibility To Submit Quotations: Interested Party, including any of its Group companies: (i) should not be engaged in betting, gambling, odds, prediction, tipping, advisory or similar services in India or anywhere in the world; (ii) should not provide any betting, gambling, odds, prediction, tipping, advisory or similar services to any Person in India; and (iii) should not have any investment or ownership interest in any Person engaged in betting, gambling, odds, prediction, tipping, advisory or similar services in India. Interested Party, including any of its Group companies, should not be directly or indirectly engaged in the business of crypto trading, crypto exchange, crypto token, virtual digital asset, Web3/tokenised products or services, or any business of similar nature as determined by BCCI in its sole and absolute discretion. Interested Party operating/engaged in multiple Brand/Product categories, one of which is relating to alcohol products or tobacco, is not permitted to submit a Quotation with respect to the Brand Categories of alcohol products and tobacco. However, the Interested Party is permitted to submit a Quotation with respect to any other non-prohibited Brand Category. Interested Party operating/ engaged directly or indirectly in online money gaming, real money gaming, fantasy sports gaming, online games involving stakes, deposits, winnings, prizes or monetary returns, or any similar product or service, whether characterized as a game of skill, game of chance or otherwise, are not permitted to submit a Quotation. To clarify, an Interested Party, including any of its Group companies, engaged or operating in any such business is not permitted to submit a Quotation. No Brand Category is blocked solely on account of an existing BCCI sponsor conflict for this new Rights cycle as of the date of this RFQ. BCCI reserves the right, in its sole and absolute discretion, to notify any additional restricted or blocked category by way of clarification, addendum or amendment prior to submission of Quotations. For the avoidance of doubt, Interested Parties may note that BCCI is concurrently conducting a separate invitation to tender for the grant of Title Sponsor Rights for BCCI Events.
